problem_statement: idangerous website-templates ships the static "Wio" app-landing HTML template, rebranded here into Wander, a fictional trail-discovery mobile app (find, save, follow and log hikes near you, with offline maps and community trail notes). The site ships two pages that share one coherent product design system: a Home page (index.html) and a Trail Journal page (trail-journal.html), both built from a shared fixed masthead nav whose every anchor carries a shared nav-link class (Download, About Wander, Features, Press, Trail Journal, Get In Touch), a shared review/feature card pattern and a shared footer. As part of the same design system the site ships a shared "Trail conditions" board (a headline, a region filter with All regions / Near me / Saved routes buttons that update a live readout, and a four-tile status strip: Open trails, Muddy sections, Closures, Fresh notes) and a shared "Live trail signals" conditions rail that is meant to appear on BOTH the Home page and the Trail Journal page so the two pages read as one system. A regression has crept into this shared trail-conditions system and must be repaired ACROSS the whole site so every page stays consistent, responsive and interactive: (1) the shared four-tile conditions strip must not overflow horizontally at 390px mobile on either page; (2) the shared conditions rail must render on BOTH the Home page and the Trail Journal page (not only on the Home page) and keep its on-system light chrome rather than collapsing into an off-system dark slab; and (3) clicking a region filter button (for example Near me) must update the shared readout to "Showing: Near me" instead of leaving it frozen on "Showing: All regions". Keep the Home overview and the Trail Journal entries intact while repairing the shared trail-conditions system.
required_content: Keep the shared four-tile Trail conditions strip (Open trails, Muddy sections, Closures, Fresh notes) free of horizontal overflow at 390px mobile on both the Home page and the Trail Journal page.

Render the shared "Live trail signals" conditions rail on BOTH the Home page and the Trail Journal page so the shared component appears consistently across the site rather than on the Home page alone.

Keep the shared conditions rail on its on-system light chrome (the shared card palette and type scale) instead of an off-system collapsed dark slab, so it stays visually indistinguishable in system from the rest of the page.
Wire the shared region filter so clicking a region button (All regions / Near me / Saved routes) updates the shared readout text (for example "Showing: Near me"), not just the active-button styling.
Preserve the existing Home overview, the six grounded Trail Journal entries and the shared masthead nav and footer chrome; do not remove sections or introduce off-system bespoke markup.
design_constraints: Repair the shared trail-conditions system in the shared stylesheet and shared script, keeping the markup identical to the rest of the design system rather than adding a bespoke one-off block.
The shared conditions rail must render on every page that carries the shared chrome (Home and Trail Journal), not on a single page in isolation.
Preserve the shared card palette, heading type scale and nav-link registry across both pages.
The four-tile conditions strip must wrap responsively so it never forces horizontal scrolling at 390px on any page.
The region filter must keep its readout in sync with the active region on click; do not ship a filter whose readout is frozen.
state_constraints: desktop_home_board verifies the shared conditions rail renders on the Home page on its on-system light chrome and the four-tile conditions strip is laid out without overflow.
mobile_home_board verifies the shared conditions strip does not overflow horizontally at 390px on the Home page.
mobile_journal verifies the Trail Journal page holds the shared design system at 390px without horizontal overflow, and that the shared conditions rail renders on the Trail Journal page too.

desktop_journal verifies the shared conditions rail renders on the Trail Journal page (cross-page consistency), the shared card grid produces at least six h3 journal entries, and the shared masthead nav and footer are present.
desktop_home verifies the shared section nav lists the Trail Journal nav-link and the Home overview is unchanged.
desktop_trailfilter verifies that after clicking the Near me region button the shared readout reads "Showing: Near me" (the interaction updates the observable terminal state).

change_completion: The shared conditions rail renders on both the Home page and the Trail Journal page and the region filter readout updates on click.
The four-tile conditions strip is laid out without horizontal overflow and the six grounded Trail Journal entries and Home overview remain intact.
design_consistency: The shared conditions rail keeps its on-system light card chrome and type scale, indistinguishable in system across both pages.
The shared masthead nav-link registry (including Trail Journal) renders consistently across the Home page and the Trail Journal page.
responsive: The shared conditions strip wraps and renders at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow on both the Home page and the Trail Journal page.
Page and card copy stay readable on mobile and tablet with no clipped content.
regression: The existing Home overview and the shared masthead nav and footer chrome remain intact.
No section is removed and no off-system bespoke markup replaces the shared design-system components.

author_notes: Repair the shared Wander trail-conditions system so every page (Home and Trail Journal) of the Wander trail-discovery site stays consistent, responsive and interactive. The reference lays the shared four-tile conditions strip out so it wraps without overflow at 390px, renders the shared "Live trail signals" conditions rail on BOTH pages on its on-system light card chrome, and wires the region filter so clicking a region updates the shared readout. INFRA (identical across reference, baseline and bad, NOT part of the graded task content): the remote YouTube iframe in the video overlay is replaced with a local static poster panel so the site serves fully offline with no network requests; each rendered section-nav anchor carries a shared nav-link class; the generic Wio template is rebranded into the Wander trail-discovery identity (masthead slogan, download copy, about copy, six feature cards, press cards, footer credit, the Trail Journal page with six grounded journal entries and its nav registration); and the shared Trail conditions board markup (region filter buttons and four status tiles) plus the shared conditions rail markup are injected identically into both pages. This infrastructure is byte-identical across all three legs. The baseline reproduces the original regression: the four-tile conditions strip is a fixed-width nowrap row that overflows at 390px mobile, and the shared conditions rail is never mounted on either page. The bad solution is a plausible-looking but wrong repair: it masks the strip overflow with overflow-x:hidden on a still-too-wide row (the document still overflows the mobile viewport), it mounts the conditions rail on the Home page only (still missing on the Trail Journal page) and restyles it into an off-system collapsed dark slab, and it wires the region filter to toggle the active button but forgets to update the shared readout so it stays frozen on "Showing: All regions". Grounding assets: i/star.png rating rows, i/logo.png masthead, i/icon.png app icon.
